2025 vs 2024 YoYIn Q4/2025, the Group reported consolidated operating revenue of Baht 966.0 million, decreased by Baht 37.0 million, or 
3.7% from Q 4/2024, mainly due to: 
Revenue from domestic sales increased from 1) A significant increase in sales from the project customers 2) Higher 
operating revenue, especially from roof structures, siding board & board, and services.
Revenue from international sales decreased from 1) The declining in international sales, particularly from Cambodia 
following border closures 2) A slowdown in orders from Vietnam and the Philippines 3) A reduction in export volumes, 
particularly from CT Tiles, siding board and board, and FC Tiles.
However, sales in Laos and Myanmar increased, reflecting the Company ’s capability to manage exports effectively 
despite external challenges.
In 2025, the Group reported consolidated operating revenue of Baht 4,531.3 million, decreased by Baht 438.6 million, or 
8.8% from 2024, mainly due to:
Revenue from domestic sales decreased  from 1) Lower selling prices amid weak consumer purchasing power 2) Stricter 
credit policies affecting certain customer groups 3) A decline in sales of AAC blocks, CT Tiles, FC Tiles, roof structures 
and OEM products, and services 4) A shift in customer behavior to reduce inventory, corresponding to the slowdown in 
the construction sector 5) The impact of a longer and more severe rainy season compared with the prior year.
Revenue from international sales decreased from 1) The declining in international sales, particularly from Cambodia 
following border closures. 
In the meantime, some parts of the revenue decline was offset by higher sales in Laos and continued growth in the 
Philippines, driven by proactive market penetration, competitive pricing, and stronger confidence in siding board & 
board, while sales in Myanmar remained stable and in line with plan, supported by a solid core customer base despite 
external challenges.In Q4/2025, the Group reported consolidated operating revenue of Baht 966.0 million, decreased by Baht 21.9 million, or 
2.2% from Q 3/2025, mainly due to:
Revenue from domestic sales decreased  from 1) Lower selling prices amid weak consumer purchasing power 2) Stricter 
credit policies affecting certain customer groups 3) The declining in sales, especially from CT Tiles 4) A shift in customer 
behavior to reduce inventory, corresponding to the slowdown in the construction sector
However, the decline in revenue was partially offset by increased sales of AAC blocks, reflecting market demand for 
cost-efficient and practical products amid a still -fragile economic recovery.
Revenue from international sales decreased from 1) A decline in demand from Vietnam and the Philippines 2) A decline
